questions.explain: The blackboard is a shared, versioned, attributed workspace (hypothesis, evidence, partial_result, critique, decision, note); the supersedes_id refinement chain keeps the snapshot at the current best understanding instead of an append-only swamp.
options: A single shared document with no versioning
A shared versioned blackboard with a supersedes refinement chain
questions.q: What is the blackboard pattern for multi-agent coordination?

questions.explain: Tasks are claimed with READPAST + UPDLOCK only when parents are done, turning the queue into a DAG scheduler; failed tasks return to pending with attempt counts bounding infinite loops.
options: Dependency-aware claiming (parents must be done) with READPAST + UPDLOCK; failures return to pending with attempt bounds
One task per agent, no dependencies
questions.q: How does the dependency-aware task queue distribute work?

questions.explain: The first agent to grab the run-scoped sp_getapplock (Exclusive, Session owner, timeout 0) becomes coordinator; if it dies, its connection drops and the lock releases for re-election.
options: sp_getapplock election on the run ID — first to grab the lock leads, death releases it for re-election
questions.q: How is the coordinator agent elected?

questions.explain: Escalating strategies: evidence-weighted voting (confidence + citations), then an adversarial round posted as a critique entry, then human escalation — with the losing hypothesis preserved in the record.
options: Evidence-weighted voting → adversarial round → human escalation, preserving the losing hypothesis
questions.q: How are conflicts between agents resolved?

questions.explain: Runs terminate on goal satisfaction, budget exhaustion (step/token/time budget — a partial answer beats an infinite run), or stagnation (no new entries in N checks); every run gets a budget.
options: Goal satisfaction, budget exhaustion, or stagnation — every run gets a budget
questions.q: What are the run termination conditions?
